yashar.name: Yashar!
yashar.summary: A new party led by former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, running together with Hili Tropper's Yesodot Yisrael party.

topics.security: Eisenkot: "There is no Palestinian state, and in the government we form, no Palestinian state will be established." According to the party's goals, Israel should pursue peace agreements and regional cooperation from a position of strength.
topics.religion: Israel as a Jewish and democratic state in the spirit of the Declaration of Independence.
topics.economy: Lower the cost of living by opening up imports, removing barriers and breaking up monopolies, and change taxation so that "work always pays more than benefits" and those who work and serve are rewarded.
topics.judiciary: A constitution including a Basic Law: Legislation, a sovereign Knesset, a government able to govern, and a strong, independent judiciary.
topics.draft: A "Service for All" law: every citizen, man or woman, serves in the IDF or in civilian service. Deferrals for Torah students and outstanding individuals only within a quota of up to 3% of each age group; for draft evaders, loss of benefits and criminal prosecution.

likud.name: Likud
likud.summary: A "national liberal movement" founded in 1973. Running together with Gideon Sa'ar's New Hope. According to the Israel Democracy Institute, Likud has not published an election platform since 2009.

topics.security: Netanyahu: "As long as I am prime minister, there will be no Palestinian state controlled by Iran – not in Gaza and not in Judea and Samaria."
topics.religion: The party's constitution seeks to instill the values of Jewish tradition in education and in the life of the state.
topics.economy: A free, competitive economy and less government involvement in the economy.
topics.judiciary: Justice Minister Yariv Levin (No. 4 on the list): "If the right wins the election, there will be different judges on the Supreme Court in the next term" and there will be "a different justice system."
topics.draft: Netanyahu: "We have not given up on the draft law" – the coalition's bill was temporarily frozen because of the war.

sourceLabels.judiciary: Yariv Levin speaking at a conference, The Jerusalem Post
sourceLabels.draft: Netanyahu's answer to a ynet question

together.name: Together
together.summary: A joint list of the Bennett 2026 party and Yair Lapid's Yesh Atid.

topics.security: Do not move from the "Yellow Line" in Gaza until Hamas is disarmed, prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, and strengthen the Abraham Accords and the alliance with moderate forces in the region.
topics.religion: A civil union law, public transportation on Shabbat as decided by each local authority, conversion by community rabbis, and an end to the Chief Rabbinate's monopoly (without abolishing it).
topics.economy: Cut food prices by 30% within three years by breaking up monopolies, removing import barriers and reducing regulation.
topics.judiciary: Adopt a constitution based on the principles of the Declaration of Independence, regulate judicial review and the Basic Laws "while seeking broad agreement," and limit the prime minister's tenure to 8 years.
topics.draft: "The Servers' Law": everyone enlists in the IDF or in civilian service, with no exemptions; cancel stipends for married yeshiva students (avrechim) and benefits for those who do not serve, and transfer the money to those who serve.

dems.name: The Democrats
dems.summary: Founded in 2024 through the merger of Labor and Meretz; defines itself as "Zionist, liberal and democratic."

topics.security: Yair Golan: "We need to decide one issue – annexation or separation"; he says an alternative to Hamas rule must be created in Gaza and that Palestinian and Jewish terrorism must be fought.
topics.religion: Golan: the next coalition should be one "that understands the separation of religion and state."
topics.economy: Fighting the high cost of living, improving welfare services and rebuilding the civil service.
topics.judiciary: Advancing a Basic Law: Legislation and strengthening the "gatekeepers" (oversight bodies).
topics.draft: "The duty to serve the state should apply to all citizens, in a state-run and equal framework"; the state should stop incentivizing non-service.

sourceLabels.security: Golan interview on "Meet the Press," N12
sourceLabels.religion: Golan interview on "Meet the Press," N12
sourceLabels.draft: Party's response to a ynet inquiry

1.name: Yair Golan
1.note: Former IDF deputy chief of staff

utj.name: United Torah Judaism
utj.summary: A joint list of the Haredi parties Agudat Yisrael and Degel HaTorah.

topics.security: Sees foreign affairs and security as a central part of its work, but also decides according to Torah considerations.
topics.religion: Preserving the religious character of the state; since 1977 it has tended to support the right-wing bloc.
topics.judiciary: According to the party, the Supreme Court has accumulated excessive power, and its powers should be re-examined and clearly defined.
topics.draft: Party chairman Yaakov Asher: "United Torah Judaism will not join a government that does not actually pass the law to regulate the status of yeshiva students."

sourceLabels.draft: Yaakov Asher statement, The Times of Israel

otzma.name: Otzma Yehudit
otzma.summary: The Israel Democracy Institute describes it as a "radical right-wing party."

topics.security: Encouraging voluntary emigration of Palestinians, disarming the Palestinian Authority, and changing the IDF's open-fire regulations and code of ethics. It presented a plan for the emigration of about 1.86 million Gaza residents within seven years.
topics.religion: Visiting the Temple Mount on Tisha B'Av, Ben Gvir said: "Jews are praying and feel that they are the masters of this place."
topics.economy: Among its coalition demands: raising soldiers' pay and giving free land to combat soldiers.
topics.judiciary: Firing the attorney general as soon as the government is formed, a Knesset hearing and a two-thirds majority in the Constitution Committee to appoint Supreme Court justices, and curbing the powers of the High Court of Justice.
topics.draft: Ben Gvir: "We have proven that Haredim can be integrated into meaningful service," through dedicated tracks in the police and the Border Police.

sourceLabels.security: Party demands at a press conference, The Times of Israel
sourceLabels.religion: Ben Gvir on the Temple Mount, The Jerusalem Post
sourceLabels.judiciary: Tally Gotliv's legal platform, The Times of Israel

1.name: Itamar Ben Gvir
1.note: National security minister in the 37th government

shas.name: Shas
shas.summary: Founded in 1984 as a national party of Sephardi Haredim, under the slogan "restoring past glory" and led by the Council of Torah Sages.

topics.security: Supports peace arrangements with Arab states and opposes dividing Jerusalem; in key votes it has taken a hawkish right-wing line.
topics.judiciary: Has not presented a detailed legal platform. Deri said he intends "to fix the justice system from the ground up and return power to the people and their elected representatives."
topics.draft: Deri: "No government will be formed in Israel with the support or participation of Shas without the status of yeshiva students being regulated."

sourceLabels.draft: Deri interview with Kikar HaShabbat, via The Times of Israel

yb.name: Yisrael Beytenu
yb.summary: Founded in 1999 by Avigdor Liberman. Opposes forming a government with Likud and the Haredi parties.

topics.security: Ending Israeli responsibility for the Gaza Strip, including closing the crossings and cutting off water, electricity and fuel supplies. According to the party, there is no point in an arrangement with the Palestinians alone.
topics.religion: Civil marriage and divorce, transferring authority over public transportation and businesses on Shabbat to local authorities, and conversion by city rabbis.
topics.economy: Less regulation, a smaller government and public sector, and breaking up monopolies, alongside topping up pensioners' income to the level of the minimum wage.
topics.judiciary: Adopting a constitution and establishing a constitutional court; opposes the "French law" and the override clause.
topics.draft: A compulsory draft law for every citizen at age 18 regardless of religion or origin, with a separate framework for Haredim and members of minorities within the Home Front Command.

joint.name: Joint List
joint.summary: A joint list of Hadash, Ta'al and Balad, first formed ahead of the election for the 20th Knesset.

topics.security: Ending the occupation and stopping the war, and establishing a sovereign Palestinian state on the June 4, 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, alongside Israel. Opposes annexation and settlement expansion.
topics.religion: Repealing the Nation-State Law and a constitutional basis of equal citizenship for all citizens, including separation of religion and state.
topics.economy: Raising the minimum wage to at least 70% of the average wage, progressive taxation, and opposition to privatizing education, health and housing. Shifting budgets from the war and the settlements to social services.
topics.judiciary: Supports reforms that strengthen democratic protections, especially for minorities, and a balanced mechanism for appointing judges that preserves judicial independence; "The justice system must protect the rights of all citizens without exception."
topics.draft: Rejects all forms of compulsory conscription, including civilian service programs, and supports free volunteering in the community.

3.name: Sami Abou Shahadeh
3.note: Former MK. Withdrew from the race on October 2, amid proceedings at the High Court of Justice to disqualify him

rzp.name: Religious Zionism and Zehut
rzp.summary: Smotrich's National Union–Tkuma and Moshe Feiglin's Zehut. The Israel Democracy Institute places it "on the far right of the political map."

topics.security: Smotrich called for applying sovereignty in Judea and Samaria "before the election" and declared: "On my watch there will be no Palestinian state. Period."
topics.religion: Strengthening Jewish education in schools and the Jewish identity and character of the state.
topics.economy: Expanding the free market and encouraging private enterprise.
topics.judiciary: Smotrich: "The election is about the justice system." The plan: an override clause with a 61-vote majority, splitting the attorney general's role and making legal advisers political appointees, and limiting interim injunctions and legal standing. Implementing it is a condition for joining the coalition.
topics.draft: Will enshrine in a Basic Law the status of those who serve in the IDF and the reserves ("whoever serves gets everything"); widening the circle of those who serve will also include drafting Haredim. Did not address sanctions on draft evaders.

sourceLabels.security: Smotrich statement, The Times of Israel
sourceLabels.judiciary: Smotrich statement and party plan, ynet

4.name: Simcha Dan Rothman
4.note: Chairman of the Constitution Committee in the 25th Knesset

raam.name: Ra'am
raam.summary: An Arab party founded in 1996; in 2021 it left the Joint List and was a member of the Bennett-Lapid government's coalition.

topics.security: Mansour Abbas reiterated his support for "recognizing the Palestinian state alongside the State of Israel."
topics.economy: Developing industrial zones near Arab communities.
topics.judiciary: The party has not presented an updated position. Abbas: "No governing authority should have absolute power"; he proposed adding opposition representatives and representatives of Arab society to the Judicial Selection Committee.
topics.draft: Opposes a law that would require young Arabs to serve; declined to address the drafting of Haredim.

sourceLabels.security: Mansour Abbas statement, The Jerusalem Post
sourceLabels.judiciary: Party position and Abbas statement, ynet

1.name: Mansour Abbas
1.note: Ra'am chairman, MK in the 25th Knesset

reservists.name: The Reservists and the Economic Party
reservists.summary: Former minister Yoaz Hendel's Reservists party (founded in 2025), on a joint list with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party.

topics.security: Working against the establishment of a Palestinian state, strengthening settlement in Judea and Samaria and "sovereignty through action" in Area C.
topics.economy: "Encouraging competition and a free market": tax benefits for companies that employ people in the periphery, removing barriers for businesses and breaking up economic concentration.
topics.judiciary: Changes to the justice system "based on broad agreement": external, independent oversight of the justice system, splitting the attorney general's roles, and a Basic Law: Legislation.
topics.draft: "Whoever does not serve will get nothing from the state": revoking the right to vote and to run for office and revoking driver's licenses, alongside service frameworks adapted for Haredim.

amcha.name: Amcha Yisrael
amcha.summary: A party founded ahead of the 2026 election by Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter.

topics.security: "A swift decisive victory, exacting a territorial price from the enemy" instead of rounds of fighting, and a voluntary emigration plan for Gaza residents who wish to leave, with international agreement. Strengthening settlement in border areas.
topics.religion: A "Jewish, Zionist and sovereign" state in which Judaism is "a family, not a battlefield"; education in Jewish values and Zionism, and no funding for schools that teach anti-Zionist content.
topics.economy: A free market, breaking up monopolies and removing import barriers and regulation to lower the cost of living; tax benefits for businesses that employ those who serve.
topics.judiciary: Splitting the attorney general's role into an independent prosecutor general and a legal adviser to the government, and establishing a "supreme court of appeal" over High Court of Justice rulings.
topics.draft: Universal compulsory service: military for those suited to it and national service for those who cannot serve in the military, with graded rewards. Tracks for "Torah excellence" will be preserved, with objective criteria for quotas of Torah students.

bw.name: Blue and White
bw.summary: A centrist party founded to bridge divides in Israeli society; the Israel Democracy Institute describes it as moderate and conciliatory on religion and state. In every poll here it is below the electoral threshold.
bw.withdrawn: On October 19, Benny Gantz announced that Blue and White will not run in the election, after it failed to pass the electoral threshold in the polls. Its ballot slip will still be at the polling station because it is too late to remove it, but the party is not running, and a vote for it will not get it into the Knesset.

topics.religion: A moderate, conciliatory approach and an empathetic attitude toward the religious and Haredi public.
topics.draft: A "Service for All" framework: every young man and woman will serve the state; economic sanctions, benefits first and foremost for those who serve, and an "exemption" only for outstanding individuals within quotas.

sourceLabels.draft: Party's response to a ynet inquiry

1.name: Benjamin (Benny) Gantz
1.note: 20th IDF chief of staff, former defense minister

צדק.name: Sharshar for Love and the Unity of the People
צדק.head: Eitan Shvili
צדק.description: A new party led by businessman Eitan Shvili ("Sharshar"), who presents himself as a candidate for prime minister and says his party will bring unity and effective governance.

ד.name: Partnership for All
ד.head: Talal al-Krenawi
ד.description: A party that has announced it will put the fight against crime and violence in Arab society at the center of its activity, and will act against home demolitions and against corruption in local authorities.
ד.note: Al-Krenawi, a resident of Rahat, was previously a member of Kadima and Labor

צף.name: The Pirates
צף.head: Ohad Shem Tov
צף.description: Part of the global Pirate movement; the party lists individual freedom, freedom of information, transparency and participatory democracy as its principles.
צף.note: Has run in elections since 2013 without passing the electoral threshold; Prof. Dan Ariely is in third place

י.name: Israel First
י.head: Sharren Haskel
י.description: A party that seeks to be a political home for the Zionist, statist, security-minded and national-liberal right, and puts the draft and equal sharing of the burden at its center.
י.note: Sharren Haskel – outgoing MK and former deputy foreign minister; the Ale Yarok party has joined the list

ה.name: Garden of Eden
ה.head: Yeshua Yisrael Ben David
ה.description: A party presenting a vision of "a government of peace, justice, freedom and abundance," centered on a "national jubilee" plan to move Israel "from a debt economy to a life economy."
ה.note: The Elections Committee rejected the ballot letters the list requested (Yod-He) and approved He alone

קה.name: Women's Voice
קה.description: A party founded in 2020 to strengthen the presence of women in politics and achieve fair representation for women in the Knesset.
קה.note: The description is from 2020, when it was led by Dr. Mazal Shaul; the name at the top of the 2026 candidate list is "Yisrael Shadmi Amir"

בד.name: Together We Will Succeed – An Arab-Jewish List
בד.head: Avi Shaked
בד.description: A joint Jewish-Arab list that holds that Jewish and Arab citizens share an interest: full civil equality, personal security in every community, and a diplomatic path to stability and peace – "not tolerance, not promises – partnership."
בד.note: Avi Shaked is a co-founder of the 888 company and previously ran for the leadership of the Labor Party

קץ.name: Fair Trial
קץ.head: Larissa Trimbobler-Amir
קץ.description: A party led by Larissa Trimbobler-Amir that demands a retrial for Yigal Amir.
קץ.note: Trimbobler-Amir is Yigal Amir's wife; in 2021 the Elections Committee did not allow "to free Yigal Amir" to be added to the list's name

נף.name: Shema
נף.head: Naftali Goldman
נף.description: A party calling for a return to a moral society, built on three pillars: community, kindness and Jewish unity.
נף.note: The platform on its website was written mostly in 2020

קך.name: New Order for a Constitution, Separation of Powers and Direct Elections
קך.head: Avital Ofek
קך.description: A list working to change the electoral and government system: adopting a constitution, separation of powers and direct elections.
קך.note: According to an earlier party platform: regional elections to the Knesset and direct election of the prime minister

זך.name: The Haredi Public
זך.head: Moti Litner
זך.description: A Haredi party that advocates protecting Torah students alongside security service in adapted tracks for those who are not studying, strengthening Haredi education and employment, and supports a free economy.
זך.note: Litner is deputy mayor of Beit Shemesh; the list has two women in its top four places

פה.name: You and Me – The Israeli People's Party
פה.head: Alon Giladi

זץ.name: Eternal Covenant for the Redemption of Israel
זץ.head: Ofer Lifshitz
זץ.description: A party calling for direct election of a president as head of the executive branch, regional elections to the Knesset, cancellation of the Oslo Accords, and applying Israeli sovereignty to Judea, Samaria and the Gaza Strip.
זץ.note: Has run in previous elections since 2006

נקי.name: Reform of the Electoral and Government System
נקי.head: Moshe Slomovich

יק.name: Gahat – The Biblical Bloc
יק.head: Moshe Lifkin
יק.description: A party calling for preparations for the mass immigration of millions of Jews to Israel.
יק.note: The description is from 2020, when it was led by Avi Lifkin; in 2026 Moshe Lifkin heads the candidate list

ז.name: Betach – Social Security
ז.head: Semion Grafman
ז.description: A social party that presents itself as representing "the citizens who carry the burden," focusing on socio-economic issues and the fight against bureaucracy and corruption, with no diplomatic agenda.
ז.note: The description is from the party's 2019 campaign; Grafman is a social activist and social media personality

בקר.name: Lights of Dawn
בקר.head: Nissim Louk
בקר.description: A party that presents itself as "a party for everyone."
בקר.note: Nissim Louk is the father of the late Shani Louk, who was murdered on October 7

נר.name: Black Color – Defender of the Torah World
נר.head: Eliyahu Eliezer Baumrind
נר.description: A Haredi party that began as an alert network against the draft, and seeks to restore the "Torato Umanuto" (Torah study as occupation) arrangement without sanctions.
נר.note: According to the report, dozens of rabbis and yeshiva heads are behind the initiative

צבי.name: Ahi Movement
צבי.head: Yuval Elmaleh
צבי.description: A list that presents itself as "the movement of the late Rabbi Yoram Abergel."

בי.name: Tzomet Beit Yisrael
בי.head: Gadi Yevarkan
בי.description: A joint list of Beit Yisrael and Tzomet, presenting itself as "the third camp on the right": a Zionist right that combines security and nationalism with socio-economic responsibility, and supports national service for every citizen.

ק.name: Tkuma
ק.head: Elkana Federman
ק.description: A new party that seeks to represent young people, the Nova community, bereaved families, and combat soldiers and reservists who, it says, have no political home.
ק.note: Federman was the security officer at the Nova festival

רץ.name: HaKahal
רץ.head: Shlomo Elboim
רץ.description: An all-Haredi party demanding that its Knesset representatives be chosen in primaries and answer to the "Kahal Council," an elected body of public representatives.
רץ.note: Elboim is a member of the Bnei Brak city council

ני.name: Noam for Israel
ני.head: Avi Maoz
ני.description: A religious-nationalist party that puts the Jewish identity of the state at its center, under the slogan "Free to be Jewish."
ני.note: Avi Maoz is an outgoing MK (the party's only representative)

whyVote.metaDescription: What happens to your vote, what happens to a blank ballot, and how many votes decided the result last time.
whyVote.title: Why vote at all?
whyVote.intro: Because your vote is worth more than it seems. Here are the numbers from the last election, and what really happens to the ballot you put, or don't put, in the box.
whyVote.statMeretzLabel: votes short of getting Meretz into the Knesset
whyVote.reason1Title: The Knesset decides things that affect everyone
whyVote.reason1P1: The Knesset that is elected will vote on the budget, the draft law, the justice system, the war and diplomatic arrangements. It also determines who forms the government. All of this will affect prices, military service, education and security over the next four years, including for those who did not vote.
whyVote.reason2Title: Elections are decided by small margins
whyVote.reason2P1: In 2022, Meretz received {meretzVotes} votes, 3.16%, and was about {meretzShort} votes short of passing the electoral threshold. Had it passed, it would have received about 4 seats, at the expense of other parties.
whyVote.reason2P2: The four parties that formed the government together received 48.4% of the valid votes, and that was enough for 64 seats, because {lostVotes} votes went to lists that did not pass the threshold and were not counted in the seat allocation. A few thousand votes one way or the other can change the whole picture.
whyVote.reason3Title: If you don't vote, you let others decide
whyVote.reason3P1: Seats are divided according to the votes of those who showed up. If half your neighborhood doesn't vote, the Knesset will reflect the other half. There is no "protest" that gets counted: whoever stays home simply does not appear in the results.
whyVote.blankP1: A blank ballot (or an empty envelope) counts as an invalid vote. It is not counted anywhere: not in the seat allocation, not in calculating the electoral threshold, and not as an official "protest." In 2022 there were {invalidVotes} invalid votes, and none of them affected the result.
whyVote.blankP2: As far as the elected Knesset is concerned, a blank ballot is exactly the same as staying home. The only difference is that it raises the turnout figure in the statistics.
whyVote.blankP3: If no party feels perfect to you, that's normal. Almost no one agrees with a party on every issue. You can choose the one closest to you on the issues that matter most to you, and a vote like that does make a difference.
whyVote.startTitle: I have no one to vote for. Where do I start?
whyVote.cardQuizText: 10 questions, and you'll see which party is closest to your views.
whyVote.cardTopicsText: What each party says about security, the economy, religion, the draft and the justice system.
whyVote.cardCompareText: Two parties side by side, issue by issue.
whyVote.thresholdNote: Mind the electoral threshold: a vote for a list that does not pass 3.25% is not counted in the seat allocation. Each party's page shows how many seats it gets in the polls.
whyVote.dayBullet1: Polling stations are open from 07:00 to 22:00, and election day is a public holiday.
whyVote.dayBullet2: You can vote only at the polling station you are assigned to, based on the address registered with the Interior Ministry.
whyVote.dayBullet3: Bring photo ID: an identity card, passport or driver's license.

towns.title: How did my town vote in 2022?
towns.intro: The official results of the last election in every city and town, compared with the whole country. Under each list it says what that list is today, because many have split or merged since then.
towns.sourceLink: Central Elections Committee final results by town
towns.sourceAfter: , which we checked against the national vote total). "Whole country" also includes double-envelope votes, such as soldiers', that are not assigned to a town. Lists that received less than half a percent in a town are counted under "Other lists." Town names in English are as given in the official file.
